Hi. I think you meant Shop····, since that's the order on your email.

It's paid and hasn't shipped yet. Your Magic M. 40T and the Harlo OS Diagnostics + 3-Month RMA plan ship November 21, from our Rotterdam warehouse.

Earlier today you asked to cancel, so I put the order on hold and nothing will ship until we sort that out. My last offer still stands: keep the order and we refund $100 to your original payment method.

Are you keeping the miner, or do you still want to cancel?
I want to cancel the order and get my money back

Understood, and I'm sorry this wait has pushed you to this point.

Cancelling isn't standard practice here, because your Magic M. 40T was built for you and is due to ship November 21. If you still want to cancel, a supervisor would have to review the request. They decide on it and get back to you with the answer.

Your order stays on hold in the meantime, so nothing will ship.

Do you want me to send the cancellation request to a supervisor?

I've sent your cancellation request for order Shop···· to a supervisor. They'll review it and come back to you with an answer by email at (email hidden)

Your order is still on hold in our store and at the warehouse, so nothing will ship while the request is being reviewed.

INSTRUCTION FROM THE HELIUMDEPLOY TEAM. Georges typed this in the team inbox. It is not a message from the customer and the customer cannot see it.
Task: Georges approved a FULL refund ($839.00) on Shop····: cancel the order with the money back to the original payment. Run the order-swap skill: approved_refund.py check --email <the order's email> --order Shop····, then approved_refund.py refund --email <same> --order Shop···· --confirmed. Only when it reports refunded: true, tell the customer it is done, the amount, and that it goes back to their original payment method, usually 3 to 5 business days to show. If it refuses or reports problems, do not say it is done: flag it and tell the customer the team will confirm the refund shortly.
Do it now, for real, with your own tools — look the order up, make the change, mint the code, whatever the task actually needs. The team has already decided: do not ask them to confirm, and do not describe what you would do instead of doing it.
Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.
If you write both a report for the team and a message to the customer, put the report FIRST and start the customer message on its own line with a greeting ("Hi <first name>,"). Everything before that greeting stays in the inbox as your note; only the greeting onward is emailed.

I've refunded Shop···· in full: $839.00 back to the original payment, with Georges' approval. The dispute check was clear and the refund tool confirmed it went through. The order now shows as cancelled and refunded with $0.00 outstanding, and I've noted the refund on the order. Nothing else needs doing on this one.

Hi,

Your order Shop···· is now cancelled, and nothing will ship. The full $839.00 has been refunded to the payment method you used for the order. It usually takes 3 to 5 business days to show, depending on your bank.

I'm sorry the wait on this miner went the way it did, and thank you for your patience while we sorted it out.

Kind regards,
Sarah
